package.experimental_setup: All three trackers were trained on the Merriwold-Dialog 2.0 training set (8,420 dialogues across five domains: hotel, train, restaurant, taxi and attraction) with 5 random seeds (seeds 1–5), identical data and the same tuning budget. Each seed fixes the data order for all systems, so seed-level results are paired. The primary metric is joint goal accuracy (JGA, %), the percentage of turns whose full predicted dialogue state exactly matches the annotation; slot accuracy (%) is also reported. The main evaluation is the Merriwold-Dialog 2.0 test set (1,000 dialogues, 7,372 turns). A secondary evaluation uses the Tarnby-Schema test set (2,140 dialogues), whose 11 services never appear in training; models are applied to it without further training. The per-domain analysis uses the single-domain dialogues of the Merriwold-Dialog 2.0 test set.

package.methods_summary: Corvane-DST is a generative dialogue state tracker that conditions slot-value decoding on natural-language slot descriptions and copies values from a compressed summary of earlier turns. Halloway-DST, a slot-gated generative tracker, is the strongest published system on Merriwold-Dialog 2.0. Pipkin-Span is a span-extraction tracker included as a lighter baseline.
package.question: How does Corvane-DST compare with Halloway-DST in joint goal accuracy on the Merriwold-Dialog 2.0 test set?

source_passages.source_title: Merriwold-Dialog 2.0: Re-annotating State Labels for Multi-Domain Task-Oriented Dialogue
source_passages.text: Version 2.0 corrects the dialogue-state annotation in 17% of turns, mostly in the hotel and taxi domains, and canonicalises 1,240 slot values such as times and prices; the 1,000 test dialogues and the train/test split are unchanged from version 1.0.

source_passages.source_title: Halloway: Slot-Gated Generation for Dialogue State Tracking
source_passages.text: Halloway encodes the full dialogue history with a shared encoder and decodes each slot value after a slot-specific gate chooses among none, dontcare and generate; we train it for 30 epochs with early stopping on development-set joint goal accuracy.

source_passages.source_title: On the Brittleness of Joint Goal Accuracy
source_passages.text: Because joint goal accuracy counts a turn as correct only when every slot matches, a single persistent error early in a dialogue can depress the scores of all later turns in that dialogue.

package.experimental_setup: All models are trained on the Harrowfield-Leaf training split (31,200 field photographs; 14 classes: 12 diseases, nutrient deficiency and healthy) with 5 seeds and evaluated by top-1 accuracy (%) on the 4,800-image test split; seed-level results are paired. Training images are stored losslessly and no compression, blur or brightness augmentation is used. Three perturbation families are applied to test images only: JPEG re-compression at quality settings 90, 70, 50, 30 and 10; motion blur with kernel lengths of 3, 7 and 11 pixels; and illumination change by scaling brightness to 0.8, 0.6 and 0.4 of the original. The project plan pre-specified the following criterion: a model counts as robust at a perturbation setting if its top-1 accuracy drops by at most 2.0 points from its clean test accuracy.

package.methods_summary: Loamwise-ViT is a vision transformer for crop-disease diagnosis from leaf photographs that uses overlapping patch embeddings and a lesion-focused attention pooling head. Ferncastle-CNN, a convolutional classifier widely used in agricultural deployments, is the main baseline; Quillon-Mix, a hybrid convolution–attention model, is a second baseline.

source_passages.text: Images were captured by extension officers with handheld phones across 41 smallholder farms over three growing seasons; each image was labelled by two plant pathologists, and disagreements (6.2% of images) were resolved by a third.

package.experimental_setup: Brackenridge-Tox and Owlery-Enc are fine-tuned on labelled comments pooled from three platforms: Gildcrest Forums (52,000 comments), Nettlebank (31,000) and Pikestaff Chat (44,000). Before training, a random 10% of each platform's comments was set aside as that platform's test split. The Cobble-Board collection (4,000 comments from a hobbyist message board, annotated under the same guideline) is the development set: it is used for early stopping, checkpoint selection and choosing each model's decision threshold. The neural models are trained with 5 seeds, and seed-level results are paired. The primary metric is macro-F1 (%) for the binary toxic / non-toxic decision; per-subtype F1 is also reported.

Owlery-Enc is a strong fine-tuned encoder baseline; Saltmarsh-LR is a logistic-regression baseline on word and character n-grams.

source_passages.text: Cobble-Board's 4,000 comments were sampled from 2019–2021 threads on model railways, knitting and amateur astronomy and were labelled by three annotators each under the shared four-subtype guideline; inter-annotator agreement (alpha) was 0.71.

source_passages.source_title: Platform Shift in Toxicity Classification
source_passages.text: Across the twelve platform pairs we examined, classifiers trained on one platform lost between 8 and 15 macro-F1 points when applied to another platform, with the largest losses for threats and identity attacks.

package.experimental_setup: Five multivariate benchmarks are used: Rookhaven-Server (server telemetry), Mallowmere-Water (water-treatment sensors), Quayside-Grid v2 (substation measurements), Tinderbox-HVAC (building climate control) and Whitlow-Rail (track-side vibration). Each method is trained on the anomaly-free training portion of each benchmark and evaluated on its labelled test portion. Detection accuracy is measured by event-F1 (%), the primary metric, averaged over 3 seeds; Dunmore-Iso is deterministic. Detection delay is the median number of time steps between an anomaly's onset and the first alarm inside it. Sprocket-AD uses an input window of 128 time steps unless stated.

package.methods_summary: Sprocket-AD is a reconstruction-based multivariate time-series anomaly detector that combines a temporal-convolution branch with a frequency-domain branch and sets alarm thresholds adaptively per series. Lanyard-TS, a transformer-based forecasting detector, is the strongest prior method on these benchmarks; Dunmore-Iso is a classical tree-ensemble isolation baseline.
package.question: Does Sprocket-AD detect anomalies more accurately than Lanyard-TS across the five benchmarks?

source_passages.source_title: Quayside-Grid v2: Revised Event Labels for Substation Anomaly Detection
source_passages.text: Version 2 relabels 14 anomaly events whose boundaries were ambiguous in version 1 and adds 6 events recovered from substation maintenance logs; scores on the two versions are not directly comparable.

source_passages.source_title: Rethinking Point-Adjusted Evaluation for Time-Series Anomaly Detection
source_passages.text: Event-F1 counts an anomaly event as detected if any alarm falls inside the event window and charges false alarms per event-free window, which avoids the inflation produced by point-adjusted F1.

For this study, both networks were also re-timed under matched conditions: the same Halcyon-G7 accelerator, batch size 1, 16-bit floating-point inference, identical 0.05 m voxelisation and the same 1,000 test scans, after 100 warm-up scans; latency includes voxelisation and post-processing. source_passages.text: Coldharbour-LiDAR contains 22,000 annotated scans from a roof-mounted 64-beam sensor recorded in four cities and labelled with 19 semantic classes; sequences 00–07 are used for training, 08 for validation and 09–11 for testing.

source_passages.source_title: Ravelin: Neighbour-Map Reuse for Sparse 3D Convolution

package.experimental_setup: Four English→X pairs are studied: Nepali (en→ne), Sinhala (en→si), Khmer (en→km) and Pashto (en→ps). Genuine parallel data come from the Fenmoor-Parl corpus; monolingual target-language text for back-translation comes from news crawls. Systems are evaluated on Fenmoor-Test (1,012 sentences per pair) with BLEU and chrF computed by the same detokenised scoring script. Each configuration was trained once (single run); the default pivot round-trip threshold is 0.4.

package.methods_summary: Wickersham-MT is a 240M-parameter Transformer translation model trained separately for four English→X low-resource pairs. We add synthetic parallel data produced by pivot-filtered back-translation, which back-translates monolingual target-language text into English and keeps only sentence pairs whose round trip through a pivot language scores above a threshold. The technique is commonly credited to Ambergate & Toivonen (2022), who are often cited for a gain of about 6 BLEU on low-resource pairs.
package.question: How do Wickersham-MT's gains from pivot-filtered back-translation compare with the improvement previously reported for the technique?

source_passages.source_title: Round-Trip Filtering for Synthetic Parallel Data
source_passages.text: For all systems in Section 5 we generated 2.1M synthetic sentence pairs with pivot-filtered back-translation, discarding candidates whose round-trip score through the pivot language fell below 0.4, and appended them to the genuine parallel data. Section 6 analyses which sentence types the filter removes.

source_passages.source_title: Synthetic Data for Low-Resource Translation: A Controlled Comparison
source_passages.text: Relative to systems trained on genuine parallel data alone, adding pivot-filtered back-translation improved BLEU by 5.8 points on average across our four low-resource pairs, compared with 2.9 points for unfiltered back-translation.

source_passages.source_title: Fenmoor-Parl: Parliamentary Proceedings for Low-Resource Translation
source_passages.text: Fenmoor-Parl aligns between 180k and 620k sentence pairs per language from regional parliamentary records; the Fenmoor-Test sets were translated from scratch by professional translators and contain 1,012 sentences per pair.

source_passages.source_title: Reporting chrF for Morphologically Rich Targets
source_passages.text: Character n-gram F-score correlated more strongly with human adequacy judgements than BLEU for the agglutinative target languages in our study.

package.experimental_setup: Thistlewood-Manip is a suite of six simulated robot-manipulation tasks (drawer-open, peg-insert, block-stack, door-unlock, cable-route, lid-twist), each with a fixed offline dataset. The main evaluation uses the standard suite with shaped rewards; a secondary evaluation uses Thistlewood-Manip-Sparse, which keeps the same tasks and datasets but replaces shaped rewards with a binary success reward. Every method is trained with 8 seeds; within a seed, all methods share the dataset shuffle and are evaluated on the same 100 fixed-start episodes per task, so seed-level results are paired. The reported metric is average success rate (%), the mean of the six per-task success rates.

package.methods_summary: Heronsgate is an offline reinforcement-learning method that penalises Q-values of actions outside the dataset's support with an uncertainty-weighted conservatism term (weight α, default 1.0). Pallister, an advantage-weighted policy-extraction method, is the strongest prior method on Thistlewood-Manip; Crumley-BC is a behaviour-cloning baseline.

package.experimental_setup: Six binary-classification datasets are used: Gorseway-Perm (membrane permeability), Hollin-Sol (aqueous solubility class), Ivybridge-Tox (cellular toxicity), Jessamine-Kin (kinase inhibition), Kelso-Brain (brain penetration) and Lumley-Metab (metabolic stability). Each dataset is divided with a scaffold split (80/10/10), so test molecules have core ring systems not seen in training. Each model is trained with 5 seeds per dataset and evaluated by ROC-AUC (×100) on the test split; hyperparameters are tuned on the validation split with the same budget for Larchmont-GNN and Quintrell-MP. Avonlea-Chem-XL is fine-tuned from its released pretrained weights.

Quintrell-MP is a message-passing network and the strongest non-pretrained baseline. Avonlea-Chem-XL, a much larger model pretrained on unlabelled molecules, is included for reference.

source_passages.source_title: Avonlea-Chem: Scaling Molecular Pretraining

source_passages.source_title: Scaffold Splits and the Optimism of Random-Split Benchmarks
source_passages.text: Grouping molecules by their core ring scaffold before splitting lowered ROC-AUC by 3 to 9 points relative to random splits across the 14 datasets we examined.
